title: I Used the Candle-Pour Table Hours on the Mentor Who Camped My Numbered Wicks

parts.text: I stepped into the pour table at 2:04 p.m. and mentor Sol was already using numbered gear. The board said: ONE TABLE. SIXTY MINUTES. WICKS STAY WITH THE SLOT. I was twenty-eight, studio secretary, holding a checkout that listed our numbered wicks. Sol shrugged. "Mentors are the wax." I photographed the board, the booking, and his leftover tabs on my numbered wicks. Then I asked for the pour log. At 2:12 the desk pinged why Sol's name was on my tabs. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The desk can see Sol's leftover tabs on my numbered wicks.

social.video_title: He camped my numbered candle wicks on my table — Part 1/2
social.description: Pour table, leftover tabs, a sixty-minute clock he posted. I logged the wicks. Would you have asked for the pour log?

parts.text: Sol called it centering until the desk asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the tab still. The wicks went back to my numbered slot. Sol ran a slot of his own and told the next mentor atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: MENTORS ARE NOT THE WAX. I keep my wicks in a labeled tin. Sol brown-bags his centering. The table finally looks like a slot, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.description: Pour log, numbered wicks, and a second line on the board. Was centering ever my tabs?
